chunks: And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

A man asked him while I was with him, and said: A Muslim man needed to sell his house, so he came to his brother and said: I sell you this house of mine, and for it to belong to you is more beloved to me than that it belong to someone else, on the condition that you stipulate for me that if I come to you with its price within a year, you will return it to me. So he said: There is no problem with this. If he brings its price within a year, he should return it to him.
I said: If there was abundant yield in it, and he took the yield, to whom does the yield belong? He said: To the buyer. Do you not see that if it were to burn down, it would be from his property?

key_terms.إِلَى سَنَةٍ: within a year, indicating the specified term of the condition
key_terms.بَيْعِ: sale or transfer of ownership through a legal transaction
key_terms.بِثَمَنِهَا: with its price, meaning the amount for which it was sold
key_terms.دَارِهِ: his house or property being sold
key_terms.غَلَّةٌ: yield, produce, or income generated from the property
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem; the transaction is legally unobjectionable
key_terms.مِنْ مَالِهِ: counted as his loss or from his property liability

ai.seo_question: In Shia fiqh, who owns the income of a house sold with a condition of return within a year?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the sale of a house with a stipulated right of return if the seller repays the price within a fixed term. It also clarifies that the property's yield belongs to the buyer during that period, because liability for loss rests upon him.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3771 - Ishaq ibn Ammar narrated from Abu Abdillah (as):

A man asked him while I was present, saying: "A Muslim man needed to sell his house, so he came to his brother and said: 'I will sell you my house. It is more beloved to me that it belongs to you than to someone else, on the condition that if I bring you its price within a year, you will return it to me.'"
He (as) said: "There is no problem with this. If he brings its price within a year, he should return it to him."

I asked: "What if the property yields a significant income during that time? Who does the income belong to?"
He (as) said: "It belongs to the buyer. Do you not see that if it were to burn down, it would be his loss?"
